summary:
plan.md is written. It describes a symmetrical, two-storey red-brick hall (33 × 17) on a grey stone plinth, with a slate civic hip roof, pavilions at the front corners and white quartz dressings. A four-column portico with a pediment carries the words TOWN HALL. A clock tower with a copper spire rises behind the portico and reads as civic from a distance. No roof dry-run or render was made. Symmetrical Victorian-Georgian brick town hall: quartz four-column portico with oculus pediment, slate hip roof, clock tower with copper spire, twin chimneys with lit campfires.
Ground: vestibule, hall with twin grand stairs, bays, two offices with fireplaces; upper: council chamber, two committee rooms, clock room, belfry.
Six parts by trade: shell, roofs, dressings, fittings/lettering, chimneys, grounds.

Masonry shell: The masonry shell is built: plinth, brick walls on both storeys, pavilions, podium, tower shaft, floors at y3, y10 and y16, partitions, two stair flights and the tower ladder. make.sh gives a whole build.nbt, and 9 of the 11 rooms are walkable (the clock room and belfry are up the ladder). I did not read the render tiles. Openings and reserved cells are left as air, along with the cells the dressings part will fill.
polish: The office doors are at x10 and x30, z16, instead of z20 as planned, because the stair flights block x11..12 and x28..29 at z18..24. Room designers should use the z16 doors.
The ladder cells at x21 z13 y27..31 show as unsupported until the dressings fill the tower's z14 wall (clock-face cells and the y27 and y31 bands) behind them.
The clock room and belfry show as unreachable in `mcd walk`, probably because it doesn't climb ladders. I did not confirm that.

Dressings have to fill the cells I left empty: the y10 and y16 wall rings, the tower rings at y27, y31 and y35, the quoin corner columns, the clock-face cells, and the y9 arch rows over the windows. They can't use over:true, since runParts refuses writes into earlier parts' cells.
Not all quoin cells are covered. I left only the corner columns empty (the 4 front pavilion corners and the 2 rear corners); the neighbouring 'long' course cells are brick.

`mcd check` also reports 6 unsupported ladder cells (the ones above) and 24 orphan blocks. Most of the orphans are smooth_quartz at x3 and z27 from the roof part. I did not investigate the 4 orphan bricks at z26 y11 (x5, x18, x22, x35).

waste.what: I worked out the window, door, arch and quoin exclusion boxes from the OPENINGS table by hand, as open() calls.
waste.cost: about 25 box calls, 1 retry because a blanket open() on the y10 string course also blocked the floor
waste.tool: A helper that reads plan.md's OPENINGS and RESERVED tables and returns an air mask, with a `wallsWithOpenings` brush that fills a wall except for those boxes.

waste.what: I found that the office doors at z20 collided with the stair flights only after `mcd walk` reported the offices unreachable.
waste.cost: 1 rebuild cycle
waste.tool: A plan-consistency check that overlays ROOMS doors on the stairFlight footprints before building.

companions.task: Lay the quoin courses in the same pass as the walls, so the mason can leave no empty cells for another part to fill.
Place the hall stairs and check headroom and doorway clearance on the ground and upper floors.

summary:
Roofs: Roofs part built: roof.json (palette-fixed, 2 north dormers) lays the civic slate hip via runParts; parts/roofs.mjs adds the temple portico gable and copper pyramid spire (scratch-built with mcd roof, copied into air only) and the lightning rod.
make.sh produces a whole build.nbt; Roofs line shows 164 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette. The roof spec dry-run has no warnings.
Still open: 3 south dormers, the pediment oculus, and the spire sits on the y35 course that is still air; the render also shows no tower shaft above the roof, which is a shell problem.
polish: South dormers: plan wants 3 on the south face (x12, 20, 28); roof.json takes one face per dormers object and the array form is ignored by the dry-run, so only the 2 north dormers are in. Add them once the spec accepts multiple faces, or via a second scratch roof.

Pediment oculus (pedimentOculus at x20, y~19 on the z6 gable) is not built: the temple gable's triangle is roof prism, so the air-only helper is refused there. Needs the roof spec to leave the gable open (gable infill) or a carve by the roofer.

Copper spire (x17..23 z9..15 y36..41) renders floating: its base at y36 sits on the y35 course, which is air until the dressings build the tower ring and the shell builds the shaft above the roof. check reports 58 FLOATING cells for it. Tower shaft cells x18..22 z10..14 y22..35 are air in build.nbt (shell side), so the spire has nothing under it yet.
Roof windows (dormer glass) and the portico tympanum colour are fittings/dressings work; the temple gable currently reads as a smooth quartz triangle from the preset.

roof.json, which sits in the shared kit rather than in my module, was edited: material ids were wrong (deepslate_tile, stone_brick) and dormers were added. The original is at /tmp/roof-part2-orig.json. Designer should confirm.
plan.md checklist 'roofs' is left unticked because of the gaps above; elements 3, 10 (partly) and 12 (2 of 5) are not ticked.

waste.what: Found the mcd CLI path and worked out the roof spec keys by grepping the toolkit source (roofs.mjs, mcd.mjs) because no spec reference lists dormers/presets/pyramid options.
waste.cost: about 8 tool calls and a 120 s stalled filesystem-wide find
waste.tool: a `mcd roof --spec-help` (or a spec-keys section in toolkit.md) listing the accepted roof.json keys, dormers shape and presets, plus the absolute mcd path in the brief

waste.what: Built the portico temple roof and the copper spire by writing each spec to a scratch file, running mcd roof on a saved copy of the build, loading the result and copying cells back into air by hand.
waste.cost: about 40 lines of glue code and a temp dir round-trip per roof; retries on the empty-grid run (failed with 'no walls found')
waste.tool: a build-library `roofInto(g, spec, box)` helper that runs the roof brush against the in-memory grid (or an option to lay a secondary roof at a given footprint and box), so no file round-trip is needed

waste.what: Tried multi-face dormers (array form) in roof.json by guess; the dry-run silently ignored it and reported only the first face.
waste.cost: 2 dry-run retries
waste.tool: `mcd roof --dry-run` should warn when a dormers entry is ignored, and the spec should accept a list of {face,count,style} objects

waste.what: Checked the spire's floating cells and the tower shaft column by reading block by block with blockAt().
waste.cost: about 30 single-cell reads in a one-off script
waste.tool: `mcd check` already reports FLOATING; a `mcd check --cell x,y,z` or a column dump (`mcd column build.nbt --at x,z --y a..b`) would show the stack at once

waste.what: Confirming which palette ids exist for the roof mix (deepslate_tile vs deepslate_tiles, stone_brick vs stone_bricks) by one-at-a-time guesses.
waste.cost: 2 wrong ids written into roof.json before `blocks --check`
waste.tool: `mcd roof --spec` should validate material ids against the palette and name the near id (the dry-run did not flag the bad ids)

companions.task: the south dormers and the tympanum: lay the south dormer cheeks and the gable infill so the oculus can be cut into a real gable panel, not a roof prism
the dormer windows (glass_pane in each 3x2 dormer front) and the portico's oculus eye
the tower shaft above the roof (x18..22 z10..14, y22..35), which is missing in build.nbt, so the copper spire has a base
a check that the spire's mix and the lightning rod meet the dressings' y35 cornice ring and the bell beam

summary:
Dressings: parts/dressings.mjs builds the mason's layer on the shell: 10 quoin columns, the y3 water table stairs, the y10 string course (flush body and rear, proud slab on the recessed front), the y16 cornice ring, four portico columns with the y15/16 entablature, tower bands at y27/31 and a proud cap at y35, four 3x3 clock faces, four belfry arches and the bell under its beam.
Built with make.sh: Dressings placed 659 blocks, 0 refused, 0 off-palette; build.nbt is whole. The front view and zooms read as a portico with a white entablature, a tower with clock and belfry, and quartz trim.
The part is done apart from the quoin long courses, which the shell blocks (see left).
polish: Quoins are corner columns only: the alternating long courses run into shell brick, which is locked, so those cells were refused inside the helper and are not in the build report. Open the long-course cells in the shell if the alternating quoin is wanted.
Tower interior at y35 (six cells beside the bell beam) is air, so the belfry ceiling is open up to the roof part's spire base; the roof part must cap it.
Orphans reported by $MCD check (smooth_quartz at y14 on x3/x7/x13/x17, bricks at y11 z26) come from the shell and the roof, not from dressings; the stub build shows 24, with dressings 20.
Water-table proud stairs and the belfry arch were not inspected at block level, only in the render.

waste.what: Cornice ring at y16 written by hand: a loop over the front (z9 pavilions, z10 body), rear z26 and side columns, cell by cell.
waste.cost: about 60 coordinates worked out by hand, one retry for the pavilion row
waste.tool: a ring/perimeter brush in the build library (box + y + per-face plane offsets) that writes air-only and returns refusals

waste.what: Working out which quoin cells the shell had opened and which long courses would be refused, by reading the shell source.
waste.cost: several minutes of reading shell.mjs open() calls
waste.tool: a refusal report from the vocab helpers (quoinColumn returns refused cells, but runParts does not surface them); a `mcd plan`-style list of shell air cells per part

waste.what: Telling my orphans from the shell's and roof's by building a stub copy of the build in a scratch directory and diffing the check output.
waste.cost: one scratch build, one check, one manual comparison
waste.tool: `mcd check --baseline stub.nbt` or a per-part attribution in the check (which part placed each ORPHAN)

waste.what: Verifying clock face and belfry orientation by eye from zoom tiles.
waste.cost: two zooms and two Reads
waste.tool: a block-level assertion per face (`mcd probe build.nbt --at x,y,z`), so that dressings can be checked without a render

companions.task: Lay the alternating quoin long courses: they need shell cells at the corners opened along each wall, and an agreed course pattern.
Check the upside-down stone_brick_stairs of the water table and the belfry arch facings at block level, since I only saw them in the render.
Check the 3x3 clock face read (white dial, black hands at y29/y30) at street distance, since the face is only 3 blocks.

summary:
Fittings and lettering: Fittings and lettering built in parts/fittings.mjs: glass in every OPENINGS window (sills on ground windows, flat arches at y9, hoods at y15), mainDoor at x20, a local rearDoor (two halves plus x20 y6 transom), and townHallLetters on the portico. make.sh left a whole build.nbt; the part reports 389 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette.
Front elevation and a zoom read correctly: every window glazed, the door whole, the Palladian window centred over it.
TOWN HALL lettering places nothing in this isolated build because the entablature is still a stub; the lettering only needs the entablature built first, which the merged run does.
polish: TOWN HALL lettering is unverified in the merged build: townHallLetters places 0 cells until Dressings builds the entablature at z6 y15..16 (in isolation the sign placed 1 wall sign once a stub was laid). Check it after the merge.
No hoods over the three upper windows behind the portico (x16..17, x19..21, x23..24): the entablature at z9 y15..16 is the hood there, so they are skipped on purpose.
rearDoor is not in vocab.mjs (plan element 18). It is a local helper: door halves at x20 z26 y4..5 facing south and a glass_pane transom at y6. The rear steps, gate and gravel path are Grounds.

Ground sills behind the portico (x16..17, x23..24 at y4, z9) project into the open porch; the plan asks for them, but they may read odd once the columns are in. Look at it when the Dressings part is merged.
The stone step outside the main door is Grounds, not built here.
Roof trim (smooth_quartz_stairs) already occupies the portico hood cells at z9 y15, so Fittings placed nothing there; the roof part, not this one, owns that row.

waste.what: Writing the window calls face by face (N pavilions, N ranges, W/E, S) and their arch and hood rows by hand: each window's at, width, y and plane typed out once per face.
waste.cost: about 30 hand-typed calls across 4 faces; the x/z ranges were copied from plan OPENINGS and checked by eye
waste.tool: A helper like openingsFromTable(g, face, plane, ranges, storeys) that reads the plan's OPENINGS rows and runs windowBay, flatArch and windowHood per storey, so the ranges live in one data table.

waste.what: Probing whether a cell held a block at all: I wrote a throwaway script with load() and blockAt() to find out what was at the entablature and hood cells.
waste.cost: 3 probe scripts and about 4 minutes of checks
waste.tool: `mcd at build.nbt x,y,z` (or `mcd cells build.nbt --box x0,y0,z0,x1,y1,z1`) printing block and state for a box, plus a refused-by-reason note from helpers that return 0 placed.

waste.what: Finding out that townHallLetters silently places nothing when its back wall is missing. The helper returns skipped:1 with a note, and only a probe with a stub revealed it.
waste.cost: 2 retries to test it with a quartz stub
waste.tool: A helper warning when a sign's back block is air, or a runParts note that names the part that owns the missing wall, so lettering that depends on another part is flagged.

waste.what: The rear door is not in the vocabulary, so I hand-wrote three g.set calls for its halves and transom.
waste.cost: 3 calls, plus a note in plan.md that is not yet written
waste.tool: A mainDoor-style helper for a rear door with transom (rearDoor in vocab/h1.mjs), so each door is one call.

companions.task: Confirm the TOWN HALL sign once the entablature is merged, choose the letter colour against the quartz, and decide whether 1 wall sign is enough or the band needs banner letters.

Review the window sills and hoods around the portico with the columns in place, so the glass, the sills and the porch read together, and decide whether the ground sills behind the portico should stay.
Hang the rear door and transom properly and add the back gate and step by the rear path, which are Grounds but meet the rear door.

summary: Chimneys and hearths: Chimneys and hearths built in parts/chimneys.mjs: two 2x2 brick stacks (x5..6 and x34..35, z17..18, y1..23) with a deepslate band at y21, a stepped slab cap at y23 and a lit non-signal campfire at y24. Four fireplaces sit in the stacks' inner columns at y4..5 and y11..12, each with a campfire at the back, a stone_bricks hearth and a brick_stairs lintel.

waste.what: Carved the four firebox openings out of the stacks' inner column by hand with a nested loop of g.set(..., air) before calling fireplace().
waste.cost: one carve loop of about 16 cell writes, plus one retry
waste.tool: A chimneyStack option (openings at the firebox rows) or a fireplace helper that carves its own firebox through the stack would remove the carve step and the coordinate bookkeeping.

waste.what: Checked the firebox and stack reading by eye from the fireplace eye view and the left elevation, not with a measured test.
waste.cost: two renders, one eye view
waste.tool: A per-part check that compares each RESERVED cell in the part's table against the built file would catch a mismatch without rendering.

companions.task: Laying the stone_bricks hearth and checking the firebox floor against the stack footing, so the hearth reads as one piece with the stack.
Checking the firebox light, since the hearth campfires are the only light in those cells and the room designers rely on them.

summary:
Grounds: Grounds part built in parts/grounds.mjs: road, sidewalk, kerb, forecourt and front steps, lamp posts, two flagpoles, door lanterns on fence posts in the porch, rear steps, gravel path with back gate, and two oak trees.
make.sh produced a whole build.nbt; the Grounds line reports 557 placed, 0 refused, 0 off-palette.
Front-left and back elevation renders show the steps, sidewalk, lamp posts, flagpoles, oaks and gate where the plan puts them.
polish: The porch podium (x15..25 z6..9, y1..3) and the step-to-porch connection are not built by this part; the plan's SITE table lists them without a part, so the shell or dressings must confirm them.
The walk was checked only as room verdicts from the entrance; no route from the street to the porch or rear door was run.
Stair tread heights follow the frontSteps helper convention (cells y1 and y2), which may sit a block off the plan's 'tread top' wording; the stair joiner should confirm.
The rear door (x20 z26) and its threshold are the fittings part's; the grounds part only builds the steps, path and gate.
The fence-gate state keys were written without checking them against `mcd states`.

waste.what: Worked out step and support heights by hand from plan.md's 'tread top at y' wording, which is ambiguous against the helper's cell convention (stairs at y1/y2 with a support fill under the upper tread).
waste.cost: about 3 minutes of reasoning and two passes of coordinates
waste.tool: A plan.md 'height convention' note (stair cell y vs walkable y) plus a helper that returns walkable cells for a stair run would have settled it without arithmetic.

waste.what: Guessed the dark_oak_fence_gate state keys (facing, open, in_wall, powered) and wrote the gate with a raw g.set, with no state lookup.
waste.cost: one call, no retry; unverified against mcd states
waste.tool: B.gate(mat, facing, open) in the build library, alongside B.fence and B.lantern, or a `mcd states` call in the recipe.

waste.what: Fence posts for the lanterns and the back-gate posts were placed one block at a time in loops.
waste.cost: about 8 set() calls
waste.tool: A fenceRun(g, from, to, axis) helper that writes posts and connection states together.

waste.what: Checked the walk by reading the room verdicts only; no walk from the street to the porch floor or the rear door was run.
waste.cost: one walk call
waste.tool: `mcd walk --from x,y,z` option for an entry point on the street, so the steps-to-porch route can be checked directly.

companions.task: Lay the front and rear stair runs and check the tread heights against the podium top at y3 and the porch floor at y4, so the step geometry is settled by someone who builds stairs for a living.
Place the four lamp posts and the two door lanterns and set their light levels, so the porch and street are lit at night.
Lay out the lawn patches, the coarse-dirt patches under the oaks, the gravel path and the back fence line, so the garden reads as planted rather than flat.

summary:
room: Vestibule: Vestibule furnished in parts/room-1.mjs: dark oak bench (two stairs, backs to the west wall) facing a lectern under a dark oak notice sign on the east wall, a red carpet runner from the door to the archway, and one hanging lantern at 20,9,12.
make.sh saved a whole build.nbt; the part placed 9 blocks with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines. `mcd room --only Vestibule` says OK: 9/9 floor cells reachable, min light 8, no dark cells.
The ladder cell x21 z13 is left clear and the lane door to archway stays open.
polish: Floor stays the shell's oak planks, not the stone floor the spec names: the floor at y3 is an earlier part's and locked.
The notice is a dark oak wall sign, not a board block; no lectern book is placed.
Shell problem outside my part: the ladder at x21 z13 (y27..31, tower interior) reports UNSUPPORTED because nothing is behind it at z14. Needs fixing in the shell.
plan.md checklist has no room rows and elements.md item 23 covers all rooms, so I did not tick it; the other room parts still need to tick it when done.
The room.png view from above does not show the interior clearly; I checked the layout by the room tool, not by eye from inside.

waste.what: Worked out the 3x3 layer rows, the lane and the light by hand from the plan grid, then re-ran make.sh and the room check to confirm.
waste.cost: about 3 make.sh runs, 2 room checks
waste.tool: A `mcd room --suggest` option that proposes furniture rows for a box and tests the lane and light before writing, so the layout is checked on paper first.

waste.what: Checked the room only from above (room.png with the roof cut away), so the lectern and the sign are hard to see and I could not judge the interior eye view.
waste.cost: 1 render, no interior check
waste.tool: `mcd rooms --eye` or an interior view flag for `mcd rooms` so the designer sees the room from the door.

waste.what: Had to look up the layers() legend format (state arrays) and the B.sign / B.lantern signatures in the build library source.
waste.cost: 1 grep of build.mjs
waste.tool: A short legend example in the toolkit reference for B.sign, B.lantern and B.stairs output.

companions.task: Write the notice board text (NOTICES, Council, Tue 10-4) as a proper hanging notice on the east wall, and decide whether a plaque or a wall board fits better than a dark oak wall sign.
Fix the shell's tower south wall at z14 (x21, y27..31): the ladder there has nothing behind it, so the ladder reads as unsupported. The stonemason would close that wall in the shell.

summary:
room: Entrance hall: Entrance hall furnished in parts/room-2.mjs: red runner on x20, two fence-and-slab tables each with a bench either side (x15 and x25, z17..23), barrels and flower pots at the back corners, two notice-board wall signs flanking the archway.
Lit by 6 hanging lanterns from the upper floor and 6 standing lanterns on the floor: $MCD room says OK, walk 199/199 reachable, min light 8, 0 dark, 0 dim.
make.sh saves a whole build.nbt (47 blocks placed for this part, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines); room.png checked from above and inside.
polish: Floor: the shell lays the hall floor at y3 (grey stone in the render), not the oak_planks the plan names. y3 is outside my box, so the oak floor needs the shell to change it.

Office doors: plan.md's rooms table puts the office doors at x10 z20 and x30 z20, but the plan grid built by the shell shows doorways at x10 z16 and x30 z16 (both walls at z20 are solid). The room check passed with the z16 doors, so the shell and the room table disagree; the integrator should settle which.
Notice boards are two generic dark_oak wall signs (NOTICES / COUNCIL), not a built board with a focal piece; the focal is the runner and the archway-to-door sightline.
Checklist: plan.md's checklist has no room rows, and elements.md item 23 covers all rooms, so I left both unticked for the integrator.
Not mine, seen in check: UNSUPPORTED ladder at x21 z13 y27..31 (tower ladder, shell) and ORPHAN bricks at x5 z26 y11 and x18 z26 y11 (shell).

waste.what: Drew the 11-row furniture grid by hand, counting characters per row; two drafts came out 17 or 18 cells wide and had to be rewritten.
waste.cost: 3 full-file rewrites of parts/room-2.mjs, about 4 minutes
waste.tool: layers() should accept sparse rows ({x: char} per z row) and pad them to the room box, so no one counts characters by hand.

waste.what: Placed the room check's suggested lantern spots (6 standing lanterns) one g.set() at a time, then reran make.sh and room check to confirm each.
waste.cost: 6 separate set() calls and 3 build cycles
waste.tool: mcd room could print the layers() rows (or a lamp layer) for its suggested spots, so the lamps can be drawn into the same text grid.

waste.what: Worked out the stair-facing and sitting directions (stair facing = high back, sitter faces the opposite way) by reasoning, to get the benches facing the tables.
waste.cost: a few minutes of reasoning, no retries needed
waste.tool: a B.bench(trade, facing) or stairs-as-seat helper in the vocabulary that states which way the sitter faces.

companions.task: Check the bench facings and the stair flights' rails beside them, so the seat-to-table sightlines are right without working out the convention each time.
Write the notice-board text and set a real board (a framed panel of signs) in place of the two generic wall signs.
Build the table and bench groups in dark oak as one kit, so every table reads as the same piece across the bays.

summary:
room: Registry bay: Registry bay furnished in parts/room-3.mjs: records counter (dark oak planks, slab top, lectern) on the hall's axis, bookshelves and barrels on the back wall, a clerk's chair behind the counter, a red runner, two candles and two hanging lanterns plus a floor lantern.
`$MCD room` says OK: 26 of 26 floor cells reachable, minimum light 8, no dark or dim cells. make.sh gives a whole build.nbt with this part's 27 blocks, no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE lines.
Interior render from the entrance reads as a clerk's counter with the lectern and shelves behind it. Structural check shows no floating or unsupported blocks in the room; the ladder and orphan warnings are in the shell.
polish: plan.md has no checklist line for the room parts and elements.md item 23 covers all interiors, so I did not tick anything there; the hall, offices and council chamber are the other designers' to tick.
The clerk's chair (dark_oak_stairs, x 14 z 11) sits behind the counter and is walled in by shelves; it is a seat for the clerk, not reachable from the patron lane, which I left deliberately.
The from-above room.png is too small to read the furniture; I relied on the room check and one eye-level render from inside instead.

waste.what: Drew the 3-layer furniture grid by hand, then fixed the light by moving one lantern after the first room check flagged two dim cells.
waste.cost: 2 make.sh runs and 2 room checks; about 6 minutes of the 12.
waste.tool: A `mcd room --apply` or `layers` dry-run that takes a light target (min 8) and proposes the lantern cells before the first build, so no rebuild is needed.

waste.what: Read the room's floor grid and light map as text and counted cell columns by hand to place each block (x mod 10 offsets, a 1-cell shift on the origin).
waste.cost: About 30 coordinate conversions worked out by hand.
waste.tool: `mcd plan --only` could print the origin and the x/z labels inside each row as coordinates, or emit a ready layers() call with the legend stub.

waste.what: Eye-level views from inside were rendered by hand with coordinates chosen by guesswork; the from-above png was too small to read.
waste.cost: 2 renders, one wasted zoom from outside the wall.
waste.tool: `mcd rooms --only <room> --eye-inside` that picks an eye point and look target inside the room box automatically.

companions.task: Check the light plan before the first build: the lantern and candle placement, so the room reaches the 8+ target without a second pass.
Set the clerk's chair (dark_oak_stairs) so it reads as a seat and sits in a lane the clerk can reach, not walled in by shelves.

summary:
room: Waiting bay: Waiting bay furnished in parts/room-4.mjs: notice board focal on the north wall between the windows, dark_oak_stairs benches on the side walls, two table-and-chair pairs, flower pots in the corners, and three hanging lanterns.
make.sh saved a whole build.nbt; the part line shows 26 placed with no REFUSED or OFF-PALETTE blocks.
`mcd room --only "Waiting bay"` says OK: 24 of 24 floor cells reachable, min light 8, 0 dark, 0 dim.
polish: The notice board is dark_oak_planks, not a readable notice: item frames aren't blocks and a wall sign can't sit on a free-standing board, so it reads as a plain panel.

Visual check was limited: room.png (from above, roof cut) is the only interior look. The eye view from the hall and the zoom from the south both showed the solid outer walls and unbuilt neighbours, not the room.
plan.md checklist and elements.md item 23 not ticked: the checklist has no room rows, and item 23 covers all interiors, so only this room is done.

waste.what: Drew the room's furniture by hand as layer rows, then rebuilt once to add a lantern the room check flagged as dim at (27,14).
waste.cost: 2 make.sh runs and 1 layer edit; coordinates worked out by hand for the benches, chairs, tables, board and lantern spots.
waste.tool: A `mcd room --lamps-apply` (or a lamp-suggestion pass before the first build) that writes the suggested lantern spots into the layer draft, plus a furniture helper for bench rows, chair-and-table pairs and board panels (benchRow/deskSet are in plan.md but not exported in the vocab).

waste.what: Looked for the room's interior by eye with `render --eye` and `zoom`. Both views from outside the building landed on the solid front wall and neighbouring stubs.
waste.cost: 3 render calls, about 3 minutes, none of them showed the room.
